facts.name: HAT-P-7b
facts.fact: Scientists have discovered a Jupiter-like planet named HAT-P-7b where it rains rubies and sapphires. It is located 1000 light-years from Earth.

facts.name: Venus Day Length
facts.fact: A single day on Venus takes 243 Earth days to complete, which is longer than its entire year of 225 Earth days.

facts.name: The Sun
facts.fact: The Sun makes up 99.86% of the mass of our solar system, and its core temperature reaches around 15 million °C.

facts.name: Collision of Galaxies
facts.fact: The Andromeda Galaxy contains over a trillion stars and is on a collision course with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.

facts.name: Supernova
facts.fact: A supernova is a massive stellar explosion that can outshine entire galaxies for weeks.

facts.name: Black Hole
facts.fact: Black holes are regions with gravity so strong that not even light can escape. Supermassive black holes can be billions of times the Sun's mass.

facts.name: Quasars
facts.fact: Quasars are extremely luminous active galactic nuclei powered by supermassive black holes.

facts.name: Neutron Stars
facts.fact: Neutron stars are incredibly dense remnants of supernovae. A teaspoon of neutron star matter weighs about a billion tons.

facts.name: Kilonova
facts.fact: A kilonova occurs when two neutron stars collide, producing heavy elements like gold and platinum and emitting gravitational waves.

facts.name: Gamma-Ray Bursts
facts.fact: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are brief but extremely energetic flashes from stellar explosions or neutron star mergers.

facts.name: Jupiter
facts.fact: Jupiter is so massive it could fit all other planets inside it. Its moon Europa may have a subsurface ocean.

facts.name: Saturn
facts.fact: Saturn’s rings span hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are only about 10 meters thick in some parts.

facts.name: No. of stars in Milky Way
facts.fact: Our Milky Way galaxy contains around 100–400 billion stars. The solar system orbits its center at roughly 828,000 km/h.

facts.name: Nebula
facts.fact: Nebula are clouds of gas and dust where new stars are born, like the Orion Nebula.

facts.name: Pluto
facts.fact: Pluto is a dwarf planet with a heart-shaped glacier region called Sputnik Planitia.

facts.name: Real Black Hole Image
facts.fact: The first-ever image of a black hole, captured in 2019, showed the event horizon of the black hole in galaxy M87.

facts.name: Exoplanets
facts.fact: Exoplanets orbit stars beyond our solar system. Some are rocky and within the habitable zone.

facts.name: Auroras
facts.fact: Auroras occur when charged particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field, creating spectacular lights near the poles.
